chunks: 2355 - Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who enters into ihram while he has game in his household, whether wild animals or birds. He said: “There is no harm.”

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; no legal objection
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: enters into the state of ihram for hajj or 'umrah

ai.seo_question: Is there any problem if a person enters ihram while there is game or birds in his household?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person in ihram who already has hunted animals or birds in his household. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that there is no harm in this circumstance, indicating that merely having such animals in one's household at the time of entering ihram is not prohibited.
